SEBoK Satellite Systems Case Study, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 4/5. The prompt-named URL Satellite_Systems_Case_Study 404s; Part 7 (SE Implementation Examples) > Space System Examples carries the discipline distributively across Hubble Space Telescope Case Study, Global Positioning System Case Study (lead authors Heidi Davidz, Richard Freeman, Alice Squires), Global Positioning System Case Study II (SoS/ESE/CSE lens), Cassini-Huygens, and Thirty-Meter Telescope studies. The Hubble study is the canonical mission-assurance worked example: an error in test fixture specification cost $1,000 to fix at design stage but escalated to $1B when corrected on-orbit, illustrating "the rising cost of defect correction through successive life cycle phases." SE-190 is the batch's V3 mission-assurance worked example: mission assurance is the highest-stakes V3-as-procedure-binding instance the corpus has read, even above SE-108 Safety, because the Hubble mirror flaw is the canonical case where virtue-based discipline (the test-fixture engineer's craft) failed and the procedural binding (independent-verification audit) failed in parallel. The Friedman-Sage nine-concept-area framework decomposes Hubble across requirements / architecture / design / V&V / risk / integration / lifecycle-support / deployment / program-management — a nine-axis Cluster A universal-sibling lattice anchored to Part 7's case-study reading discipline.

II. Source Read

Part 7 — Systems Engineering Implementation Examples > Space System Examples. Hubble case study uses the Friedman-Sage framework, decomposing across nine concept areas: requirements definition, systems architecture, design, verification/validation, risk management, integration, life cycle support, deployment, program management. Hubble's five lessons learned: (1) stakeholder engagement throughout, (2) pre-program trade studies exploring diverse alternatives, (3) systems integration as fundamental resource requirement, (4) life cycle support designed from concept phase, (5) risk management with clear contractor/government oversight. Verbatim mission-assurance datum: a test-fixture specification error cost $1,000 to fix at design stage and escalated to $1B when corrected on-orbit, illustrating "the rising cost of defect correction through successive life cycle phases." GPS Case Study (1960s concept studies through 1995 Full Operational Capability) supplies four learning principles: enabling individuals (staff key positions with domain experts), configuration management (rigorously maintain program baselines), enabling the organization (high-level support and advocacy for funding stability), risk management (disciplined throughout life cycle). GPS II reads through SoS/ESE/CSE lens; key lessons include communications fostering, skilled personnel, signal-structure-in-space integration strategy, and the Joint Program Office (JPO) resolving inter-service rivalries.

III. Structural Read

Cluster K V3-as-procedure-binding at mission-assurance, batch's worked example, strongest stake yet read. The Hubble mirror flaw is the canonical case where V3 failed on virtue-alone: the test-fixture engineer's craft was insufficient and the independent-verification audit failed in parallel. The $1K-to-$1B cost-escalation is the V3-failure cost-curve: when V3 binding fails at the early-rung, the cost-of-failure compounds across all subsequent rungs. SE-190 supplies the strongest mission-assurance worked example: mission-assurance V3-binding is structurally similar to safety V3-binding (SE-108) but at orbital-recovery-impossibility stakes, where post-deployment correction is bounded by physical access. V3 sub-mode candidate: mission-assurance-binding, tenth sub-mode candidate after the nine surfaced through SE-185 / SE-186 / SE-187 / SE-188.

Cluster A universal-sibling lattice, Friedman-Sage nine-concept-area framework, N=9. Requirements / architecture / design / V&V / risk / integration / lifecycle-support / deployment / program-management is a clean N=9 universal-sibling lattice at the case-study-reading rung. Convergent with the §VII.7 N≈10 marker; the Friedman-Sage framework is structurally an N≈10 instance at the case-study-reading discipline. SE-190 supplies the second clean N≈10 instance after SE-135 MBSE Process paired-parallel (Properties × Criteria); the N≈10 marker reaches fifth load-bearing instance.

Cluster F backward-pulverization with cost-curve extension. Hubble's $1K-to-$1B escalation IS the cost-curve of pulverization-failure: when the substrate is not adequately pulverized backward at the early rung, the forward composition compounds the failure cost. The Cluster F reading is sharpened: backward-pulverization is V3-binding's mechanism, not merely a structural decomposition. SE-190 surfaces backward-pulverization-as-V3-mechanism as a sub-form candidate.

Cluster I pin-art / temporal-concurrency at lifecycle-support-from-concept. Hubble lesson 4 ("life cycle support designed from concept phase forward") is pin-art at the lifecycle rung: the concept-phase decision determines what is recoverable at the operations-phase. This is the same form as SE-044 Process Concepts but at the engineering-decision-temporal rung; convergent with SE-185's pin-art reading.

Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument with case-study sub-pattern. Part 7 distributes its satellite-systems content across multiple case studies (Hubble, GPS, GPS II, Cassini, Thirty-Meter Telescope) without a synthesis "Satellite Systems Case Study" anchor article. This is structurally the same as Cluster J D8 internal-migration but with a case-study-cluster sub-pattern: the discipline (read satellite SE through implementation examples) is constituted by the cluster of case studies, not by a single anchor.

Cluster B multi-keeper composition at JPO contractor/government keeper-pair. GPS lesson 4 (risk management with contractor/government oversight) and GPS II's JPO-as-rivalry-resolver name the multi-keeper structure: prime-contractor-keeper, government-program-office-keeper, and the federation-keeper (JPO) that composes them at the program rung.

V. Residuals

Case-study-cluster sub-pattern of Cluster J D8. Part 7 hosts distributed case studies under topical groupings (Space System Examples here, with health/medical/transportation analogs in other groupings). The case-study-cluster is a fifth dispersion mode beyond the §VII.7 four-mode taxonomy (bidirectional-fold / internal-migration / external-migration / dual-discipline-distribution). Worth flagging.
